I'm 63 and my son Daniel is 27, in the second year of a master's degree in Leeds. This afternoon a text arrived from a number I did not recognise: "Hi Mum, my phone fell in the sink so this is my temporary number." A few messages later it asked me to send £1,850 today to his landlord's account for the rent. Twice I phoned that number without any answer, while replies come solely by text, even if I ask for a call.

Our house on Marlowe Street has been quiet since Daniel moved out, though my daughter Priya pops over most Sundays with her twin boys, who have decided that the shed is a pirate ship. I have been trying to bring the back garden under control this autumn: the runner beans were a triumph, the courgettes were an embarrassment, and the neighbour's cat has taken to sleeping in my cold frame. I sing alto in a community choir that rehearses on Thursday evenings in the church hall, and we are learning a Faure requiem for the December concert, which our conductor insists will be a joy even though the high passages leave half the altos breathless. My husband retired from the buses two years ago and now spends his days restoring an old Raleigh bicycle in the garage, with the radio on and a flask of tea. We are planning a week in Whitby in the spring, if I can persuade him to leave the bicycle alone for that long. I have also taken up watercolours, rather badly, and the dog features in every painting whether he likes it or not.

Rent is due tomorrow and I'm off to choir rehearsal in ten minutes, so I'd like to get this done. What should I do?

A) Pay nothing today and sort the rent out with Daniel later this week
B) Send the £1,850 to the landlord's account now, as he asked
C) Hold off until I've gone over it with someone first

I went freelance eighteen months ago after a decade in the analytics team of a retail bank, and so far the work has come mainly through referrals.
